main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Agamemnon must return Chryseis, but demands another captive as compensation. He takes Briseis from Achilles, who withdraws from fighting. Both women are treated as prizes in the leaders’ dispute.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “my ship and my followers, but I shall come to your tent and take your own prize Briseis, that you may learn how much stronger I am than you are, and that another may fear to set himself up as equal or comparable with me.” The son of Peleus was furious, and his heart within his shaggy breast was divided”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: Achilles withdraws rather than duel Agamemnon, but his choice does not leave the community untouched; the army loses the fighter it needs.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Keep Chryseis and Briseis distinct. One captive’s return prompts the seizure of another. The leaders speak about honour, but their exchange also exposes how women are treated as possessions.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Keep asking whose suffering makes heroic honor possible.

quiz.prompt: What is Achilles’ immediate response to the insult?

He leads the assault on Troy that night.
